newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian prosecutor fears unrest in jails.
newsitem.headline: Russian prosecutor fears unrest in jails.

text.p: Appalling conditions in Russian prisons could provoke a "social explosion" among inmates, Prosecutor General Yuri Skuratov said on Monday.

Skuratov painted a picture of misery and tension in the prison system at a meeting of security officials which decided to send a report on the situation to President Boris Yeltsin, parliament and the government.
"If we do not take urgent measures, it (the situation) could provoke a social explosion," Skuratov told the meeting in comments broadcast by Russian television.
"It is clear that those who have been convicted have every reason for discontent."
Interfax news agency quoted Skuratov as saying the situation at detention centres, where people are held before trial, was also dire.
It was unacceptable that some people stayed in these centres for two to three years, longer than the law permits, while courts considered their cases, Skuratov said.
He said more than one million people were held in Russian detention centres and corrective camps and he was worried about overcrowding.

He expressed particular concern at the rising incidence of illness. About 2,000 people died of tuberculosis in prisons last year and the death rate from the disease was 10 times higher than the average rate in Russia, he said.
The meeting was attended by officials from the government, the Supreme Court, the interior ministry and the Federal Security Service.

RIA news agency said Skuratov had demanded that prosecutors ensure a more balanced approach to choosing means of punishment when jailing offenders and urged them to ensure red tape is reduced to a minimum in investigating criminal cases.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted deputy interior minster Pyotr Mishchenkov as telling the meeting that 100 people employed in the criminal justice system had committed suicide last year.
The main reasons for falling standards and disillusionment, Mischchenkov said, included delays in wage payments to people employed in prisons and difficulties they face with housing.
Russia has faced a surge in organised and violent crime since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991 but few major cases are solved.
Skuratov has regularly been ridiculed by the media for failing to solve a growing number of murders of prominent people including businessmen, politicians and journalists.
